statement: For the exact 24-vertex, 36-edge labeled graph T in problem.md, the family M(T) of five-edge sets F satisfying gamma(T-F)>gamma(T) has cardinality 276. The full abstract automorphism group Aut(T) has order 48, and M(T) has exactly eight orbits. Under the lexicographic canonical convention of problem.md, their representatives, orbit sizes, setwise stabilizer sizes, and gamma(T-F) values are: [(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(1,4),(1,5)]: (24,2,9); [(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(1,4),(4,9)]: (48,1,9); [(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(2,6),(2,7)]: (12,4,9); [(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(2,6),(8,14)]: (48,1,9); [(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(5,10),(5,11)]: (48,1,9); [(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(5,10),(8,14)]: (24,2,9); [(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(6,11),(6,12)]: (48,1,9); [(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(6,11),(7,13)]: (24,2,9). These disjoint orbit sizes sum to 276; in particular, every member of M(T) contains the complete three-edge star at some vertex.
contribution: This exact exhaustive classification answers the full finite question frozen in source.md and strictly strengthens the nearest primary result, which proves gamma(T)=8 and b(T)=5 but gives only one five-edge witness. The contribution claimed is the 276-set, eight-orbit classification and exact post-deletion domination values, not literature-wide priority or a new general bondage theorem.
